title: Targeted Gene Sequencing Using LR-PCR-NGS Approach
author: Sathiya Maran
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbjtiknn
materials: DNA thermal cycling was performed using a SureCycler 8800 (Agilent Technologies, UK); 94°C for 2 min, 94°C 12 sec, annealing temperature for 30 secs, 68°C for 10 mins, 68°C for 7 mins for a total of 35 cycles. The size of the amplified PCR products was determined by gel electrophoresis using SYBR® Green I nucleic acid gel stain (Life Technologies, USA) under ultraviolet light. The amplified products were then purified by using an Illustra Exo-ProStar (GE Healthcare, UK). Subsequently, the LR-PCR fragments were quantified using Qubit® 1.0 Fluorometer (Invitrogen, USA) with Qubit dsDNA BR Assay Kits (Invitrogen, USA) and were pooled together at equal molar ratios.

The identified variants were also genotyped in the control population either by made-to-order TaqMan SNP Genotyping Assay (ThermoFisher, USA), custom TaqMan SNP Genotyping Assay (ThermoFisher, USA) or Sanger sequencing, based on the manufacturer’s protocol.
Modelling of the mutant protein structure

steps.title: Extract Genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Extract genomic DNA from patient samples using the appropriate kit based on sample type.

substeps.instruction: Extract DNA from peripheral blood (n=48) using GeneAll® ExgeneTM Blood SV mini (GeneAll, Korea).
Extract DNA from saliva (n=29) using PSP® SalivaGene DNA kit (STRATEC).
Measure the concentration and purity of the extracted DNA using NanoQuant (Tecan, USA).

steps.title: Perform Long-Range PCR (LR-PCR)
steps.instruction: Amplify the MYH3 gene regions using LR-PCR based on the Ensembl Genome Browser sequence (ID: ENSG00000109063, GRCh38).

substeps.instruction: Design primers to target the entire promoter, 5’ and 3’ untranslated regions, and coding regions.
Perform four distinct LR-PCR reactions using Max Taq Polymerase (Vivantis, USA) according to the manufacturer's protocol.

steps.title: Prepare Indexed Paired-End Libraries
steps.instruction: Generate libraries from pooled LR-PCR products using the Nextera XT DNA Sample Preparation Kit (Illumina, San Diego, CA) per manufacturer's protocol.

substeps.instruction: Use 5 µl of pooled LR-PCR products (at 0.2 ng/ul, totaling 1 ng) per sample.
Ascertain library fragment length using the High Sensitivity DNA kit (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA) on a 2100 Bioanalyzer (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA).

steps.title: Sequence Libraries on MiSeq
steps.instruction: Perform a 300-cycle sequencing run on the MiSeq (Illumina, San Diego, CA) using the MiSeq Reagent Nano Kit v2 (Illumina, San Diego, CA).

steps.title: Process and Analyze Sequencing Data
steps.instruction: Evaluate raw data and identify variants using a bioinformatics pipeline.

substeps.instruction: Perform quality control on raw data using FastQC (version 1.0, Babraham Bioinformatics, UK).
Align reads to the hg19 reference genome using the BWA-MEM (version 1.0) algorithm with default settings.
Filter SNPs and use Variant Studio v2.1 (Illumina, San Diego, CA) to identify and annotate exonic and intronic variants and check public databases.
Examine read counts of target amplicons and confirm variants using Integrative Genomics Viewer (IGV version v1.0.0).
Resequence all identified variants using Sanger sequencing.

steps.title: Perform In-silico Pathogenicity Analysis
steps.instruction: Predict the potential impact of identified non-synonymous variants.

substeps.instruction: Predict pathogenic potential using SIFT (scores < 0.05 suggest non-tolerated change) and PolyPhen-2 (scores > 0.85 'probably damaging', 0.15–0.85 'possibly damaging').
Analyze evolutionary conservation using the Clustal Omega programme (EMBL-EBI).
Predict splicing effects using Human Splicing Finder (HSF) version 3.0 and ESEfinder 3.0.

steps.title: Perform Homology Modelling
steps.instruction: Model the structural impact of mutations on the MYH3 protein.

substeps.instruction: Align wild and mutant complete MYH3 sequences against the Protein Data Bank (PDB) to select templates; identify PDB ID: 5TBY (72% identity) and 5WJ7 (83% identity) as suitable templates.
Build 20 models for wild and mutant type sequences using Modeller 9v20.
Select the best models based on the lowest discrete optimize potential energy (DOPE) scoring.
Calculate structural differences between mutant and wild type models using the root mean square deviation (RMSD) method.
